subject: Interop qualification: p95/p99 & tokens/sec probe for Edgewise
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@edgewise.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-04-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — follow-up and proposed interop probe

Hi Tim — great to chat earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the scope of the A/B probe we discussed (Redwood vs. Hyperscaler endpoints):

Summary of ask:
- Edgewise wants p95/p99 latency and sustained tokens/sec comparisons for two traffic shapes: (a) short-chat bursts (mean tokens/resp ~ 120) and (b) long-context summarization (tokens ~ 1,200).
- Measure both cold-start and steady-state under continuous load for 30m windows; capture KV cache hit behavior.
- Test contexts at 128 and 512 prompt lengths; report p50/p90/p95/p99 and tokens/sec at endpoints.

What we’ll run (proposed):
1) Controlled A/B test: same prompt set sent concurrently to Redwood hosted inference and to the hyperscaler endpoint you mentioned (we'll need their endpoint + auth).
2) Two model variants: base FP16 and quantized int8 (if you permit quantized runs).
3) Instrumentation: p95/p99, tail latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), error rates, and request/response sizes.

What we need from you:
- Sample prompt set and representative token distribution (or a small corpus) — we can anonymize.
- Hyperscaler endpoint details and any rate limits/ingress constraints.
- Confirmation you’re OK with us storing traces for 30 days for analysis (we can redact PII).

I attached a short lab scope (redwood-lab-scope.pdf) and a drive folder with the initial workbook. Proposed window: next week Tue/Wed (2029-04-09/10). Are you available for a 30-min kickoff?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate schedule once I have confirmation.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
naomi@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0119

Attachment: redwood-lab-scope.pdf (4 pages, scope + metrics)
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@edgewise.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-04-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — follow-up and proposed interop probe

Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. That scope looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- We'll share a 2000-row prompt sample and an anonymized trace (request/response sizes). Expect that in a separate S3 link by EOD tomorrow.
- Hyperscaler endpoint: currently using HyperCloud AI managed endpoint (svc-edgewise@hypercloud, token-based). We'll send connection details via our security mailbox (security@edgewise.com) once NDA/PoP confirmed.
- We prefer that quantized runs be labeled clearly in the report — procurement cares about quality regressions.
- Retention: 30 days is fine; we need a short attestation for our security team confirming traces will be redacted.

Given procurement timelines, if the numbers look favorable we may accelerate a Dedicated trial. Can you include p95/p99 across both small-burst and long-context flows per your plan?

I can do the kickoff 2029-04-09 at 10:00 PT.

—Tim
Tim Jenkins | Principal Architect
Edgewise Systems
tim.jenkins@edgewise.com | +1 (206) 555-0182
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@edgewise.com>
Date: 2029-04-03T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick sync — follow-up and proposed interop probe

Ben/Jonas — forwarding Tim's confirmation. Action items for the Redwood test plan (I’ll own coordination with Edgewise):

1) Test matrix (please confirm availability):
   - Models: rwd-2.1-fp16, rwd-2.1-int8
   - Context: 128 / 512 / long (1,200 tokens)
   - Traffic: small-chat burst (theta=120) and long-run summarization (continuous 30m load)
   - Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99, tokens/sec sustained, server-side CPU/GPU utilization, error rate, median token generation time

2) Hyperscaler parity: we need to ensure identical prompt encoding and tokenization before A/B. Jonas — can you confirm tokenization parity script is ready? Ben — can you prepare the runbook (interop-test-runbook.md) and the quantized variant performance knobs?

3) Security / compliance: Tim asked for a redaction attestation. I'll prepare a short note. Also confirm we have an NDA/PoP template to share with Edgewise security.

Schedule: kickoff 2029-04-09 10:00 PT (confirmed by Tim). Let's lock the lab run for Tue afternoon PT and Wed morning PT if needed.

If we can get the S3 prompt sample by tomorrow, we can finalize the workload and pre-provision test keys.

—Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@edgewise.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-04-05T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Interop test runbook + schedule

Tim — thanks again. Attaching the runbook and a short checklist to make the test reproducible on both sides. High level:

- Kickoff: 2029-04-09 10:00 PT (30m) — align on endpoints, auth, and prompt sample delivery.
- Day 1 (Tue afternoon): short-burst A/B runs (5x 30m windows), cold vs warm.
- Day 2 (Wed morning): long-context continuous runs (1x 30m) and quantized int8 evaluation.
- Deliverables: CSV with per-request latencies (ms), tokens/sec timeline, and a 2-page readout with p95/p99 and tail analysis.

Quick checklist for Edgewise security:
- Share endpoint URL + token for hyperscaler (scoped test token).
- S3 link to anonymized prompt set.
- Approval for us to store anonymized traces for 30 days.

Attachments: interop-test-runbook.md (Markdown runbook, contains commands, measurement scripts, and expected output formats).

If this plan looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite and pre-create the test harness keys.

—Ben
